text:
Maya: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting p95 jump right after today's runtime rollout (v12.2). Seen p95 ~1.1s from baseline ~320ms for text.generate on medium-length prompts. Acme-inc hit it repeatedly. @Jon can you triage?

Jon: On it. Do we have deploy logs / which cohort was canary? Any obvious config changes called out in the rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout /deploys/runtime/v12.2 -> 100% at 11:02 UTC. Canary 10% -> 25% -> 100% (no automated rollback triggered). Diff summary: kernel-selector threshold tweak + default quantization flag enabled for gpu-opt modules.

Support: attaching two sample request ids that repro consistently from the customer: req_acm_001, req_acm_002. Repro steps: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"<~300 tokens>"}'` — p95 spikes for us within 30s of request bursts.

Samir: I pulled traces for those request ids. Root cause looks like increased queue_ms before execute for some hostgroups. Queue times for tails jump ~120ms -> 900ms. Not seeing errors, just long queue/execute windows on hotpath.

Jon: Quick snippet from trace dump: ```log
req: req_acm_001
latency_ms: [115, 130, 120, 980, 1100]
queue_ms: [9, 11, 8, 480, 520]
worker: gpu-45
kernel: gemm_v2_opt_threshold
``` Suggests kernel selector chose a slower path for certain sequence lengths / batch sizes.

Maya: Hypothesis: v12.2 changed kernel-selector threshold so some small-batch requests are routed to the fused kernel that has poor latency for our micro-batching pattern. Also quant flag changed. Both could affect perf. We should bisect between those commits.

Samir: Agreed. Temporary mitigation: split routing — route affected tenant cohort back to v12.1 (old selector) while we validate. I can flip routing for acme-inc now to 12.1.

Jon: I'll add a fast-change config to force legacy kernel on the fleet for the next hour: `KERNEL_FORCE=legacy` at service-config. Doing a hotpatch and monitoring. Will also open a PR to revert the quant flag default.

Samir: Rollback/reroute done for acme-inc. Early telemetry: p95 for their requests dropped from ~1.1s -> 340ms within two sampling windows. :thumbsup:

Maya: Nice. Next steps: 1) Bisect kernel-selector change vs quant default (assign). 2) Add more granular telemetry (kernel used, batch_size, seq_len) to per-route logs. 3) Hardening: don't select fused kernel for batch_size <= 4 unless latency profile matches.

Jon: Bisect plan: reproduce locally with perf-runner using customer payloads across seq_len 128–1024, batch sizes 1–8. Commands: ```bash
./tools/perf-runner --requests requests_acme.json --kernel-variant candidate --runs 50
``` If we reproduce, we narrow commits.

Kevin: I'll take the bisect. Starting with the two suspect commits (kernel-selector change and quant-flag default). Will iterate with the perf-runner and post results here.

Support: Thanks. I'll let customer know we routed them back and we're running a bisect; will offer a temporary SLA credit if tails keep being noisy.

Jon: FYI adding an alert rule to catch kernel-selection tail increases across tenants so we catch this earlier.

Samir: Noted — also adding a per-hostgroup queue_ms heatmap to the console.

Maya: Great. Keep updates here. If bisect reproduces, we should fast rollback the selector change (or add the batch-size guard) before any wider rollout.

Kevin: First bisect pass complete — reproduces when `kernel-selector` picks `gemm_v2_opt_threshold` for seq_len 768 with batch size 2. Narrowing to exact patch. Will post commit hash in ~30m.

Maya: Perfect — thanks everyone.
